title: 95% of Vietnamese Want the Trade to End. So Why Hasn't It?
excerpt: A 2021 survey found overwhelming public support for ending the dog meat trade in Vietnam. The barriers are political and economic — not cultural. Here's what's standing in the way.
body_html:
The data is unambiguous: 95% of Vietnamese respondents in a 2021 survey support ending the dog meat trade, explicitly rejecting the idea that it is a cultural necessity. This is not a fringe position — it is a supermajority mandate.

So why does the trade persist? The barriers are structural, not cultural. A small number of economic actors — traders, transport operators, and informal slaughter operators — have an active financial interest in maintaining the status quo. Without formal regulation, there is no mechanism to enforce a ban even if one were enacted tomorrow.

Political momentum has been slow. Local governments in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have issued advisory recommendations to reduce dog meat consumption, citing public health risks and international scrutiny. But advisory recommendations are not law, and enforcement is non-existent.

The path to change runs through the Communist Party of Vietnam and food safety authorities — the bodies with actual regulatory power. A sustained, locally-led campaign applying public pressure through formal petition channels is the most effective lever available.

This campaign exists to be that lever. Sign the petition and join the 95% who are already on the right side of this issue.
author: SDE Research Team
